newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Spice Telecom launches cellular service.
newsitem.headline: India's Spice Telecom launches cellular service.

text.p: Spice Telecom, a joint venture between Motorola, Hong Kong's Distacom and India's Modicorp, launched its cellular telephone services on Thursday.
"Through Spice Telecom we hope to bring leading technologies and world class customer care to the doorstep of customers," Spice Telecom chairman B.K. Modi said while lauching the service.
Modi, one of India's biggest tycoons and a Buddhist, chose the Buddha's birth anniversary to launch his group's digital communications venture.

Spice Telecom is one of many cellular operators that have been awarded licences under an economic liberalisation programme begun by the government in 1991. Two cellular services licences were auctioned for each of India's 16 zones in 1994.
Spice holds licences for the zones of Karnataka and Punjab, two of the economically strongest parts of India.
The Karnataka zone includes Bangalore, India's fastest growing metropolis, where Spice launched its service. Punjab, India's bread-basket, has the highest per capita income in the country.
A company statement said Spice hoped to have 105,000 cellular subscribers in Punjab, and 130,000 subscribers in Karnataka within three years.
Spice has a paid-up capital of $96 million. Distacom holds 39 percent of the venture's equity, Motorola 10 percent, and Modicorp 51 percent.
Company officials say that over a three-year period the company will invest $280 million in rolling out the network. Motorola and Siemens AG are the prime suppliers for Spice's network.
